title: Wendell and the Sigil Again
premise: Mara Lockridge fled her hedge-witch mentor ten years ago and built a small, safe life selling charms in Ashmoor, a city where magic is outlawed. When her date Wendell turns out to be the 'Sigil' named in a century-old prophecy, both are dragged into a war between the surface guilds and the court beneath the mountain, where Mara's long-lost brother's soul has been sold as payment for a bargain she unknowingly triggered. To save him, Mara must reclaim the stolen sigil-stone, confront the mentor she abandoned, and choose whether to wield the prophecy's power herself. In the end she shatters the stone rather than claim it, buying her brother's freedom at the cost of her own magic, and finds her true family in Wendell and the ragged allies who chose to stay.
about_author: Cyrus Okafor is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing grimoires in a university basement before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about reluctant magicians and the families we build when the old ones fail us.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Tuesday
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A quiet night selling luck-charms in Ashmoor's night market, establishing her careful, hidden life and her rule never to touch real magic. Her date Wendell arrives, awkward and earnest. Beat: longing for connection while keeping every wall up.

chapters.title: A Face in Old Vellum
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell, a rare-book appraiser, recognizes Mara's face in a century-old prophetic text he's cataloguing — her name, her scar, tonight's date. He brings it to her half as a joke. Beat: the uncanny crack in ordinary life.

chapters.title: Ink That Moves
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The prophecy's ink crawls and pulls them both into the book's world: a frozen crossroads where a hooded figure names Wendell 'the Sigil' and demands the stone. They barely escape back. Beat: terror and unwilling wonder.

chapters.title: What the Guild Knows
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The mage-hunting Guild raids Wendell's shop, having sensed the prophecy's activation. An old guildsman, Corvane, offers to protect Wendell — if he surrenders Mara. Beat: betrayal dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: The Brother She Buried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara deciphers the prophecy's margins and learns her brother Tam, lost ten years ago, is alive — his soul sold to the Undercourt as part of her apprenticeship bargain. Beat: guilt ignites into purpose.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Mara and Wendell descend through a smuggler's door into the mountain's under-city, guided by Nix, a pickpocket who deals in stolen names. Beat: found family's first fragile spark amid danger.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They witness the Undercourt's splendor and cruelty: souls bound as living lanterns. Mara glimpses Tam among them, hollow-eyed. Beat: horror that hardens resolve.

chapters.title: Bargaining With Hungry Things
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell, as the Sigil, can open the court's vault — but the Underqueen offers him power in exchange for Mara. He refuses, and they flee with only a fragment of the truth. Beat: loyalty tested and proven.

chapters.title: The Mentor in the Marsh
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To learn how the original bargain was made, Mara must return to the mentor she abandoned: old Sef, exiled in the marshes. Their reunion is acid and grief. Beat: confronting the past she fled.

chapters.title: Sef's Confession
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef reveals he sold Tam's soul to save Mara from the prophecy's first claiming — and that the sigil-stone was split, half buried beneath Ashmoor's Guildhall. Beat: forgiveness refused, understanding earned.

chapters.title: The Guildhall Job
chapters.summary: Nix's POV. The crew — Mara, Wendell, Nix — plan the impossible: steal the stone-half from the Guildhall during the Binding Festival. Beat: camaraderie and heist-morning nerves.

chapters.title: Festival of Chains
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The heist begins amid the festival; Mara disguises herself as a Guild acolyte and walks the halls where she was once nearly caught. Beat: tension, and the seduction of belonging to the powerful.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Corvane corners Wendell, revealing the Guild plans to use the stone to enslave the Undercourt's souls — and offers Wendell a place at Corvane's right hand. Beat: power's corruption whispers sweetly.

chapters.title: The Stone in Hand
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara seizes the stone-half, but touching it floods her with the prophecy's power and vision — she could remake everything. She barely hands it off before it claims her. Beat: temptation at its peak.

chapters.title: Nix's Price
chapters.summary: Nix's POV. The Guild captures Nix, who traded information for a promised pardon — and then discovers the pardon was a lie. Nix escapes and warns the others, choosing them over safety. Beat: found family sealed in fire.

chapters.title: The Second Half
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The stone-half resonates: the other half is the Underqueen's crown-jewel. The only way to free Tam is to bring the halves together in the Undercourt — exactly what the prophecy wants. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: March Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The company descends openly, gathering Undercourt outcasts as allies. Wendell accepts what the Sigil is — not a weapon but a key. Beat: resolve and quiet courage.

chapters.title: The Underqueen's Court
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Confrontation with the Underqueen, who reveals the prophecy's author was the first soul she ever took — and that the stone, made whole, will make its bearer a god or a lantern. Beat: the true stakes revealed.

chapters.title: The Choosing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell takes the stone to buy time, and its power begins remaking him — colder, grander, crueler. Mara reaches him not with magic but with memory. Beat: love as anchor against corruption.

chapters.title: Shatter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, climax. Rather than let either side claim the whole stone, Mara pours her own magic into it and breaks it. The souls go free — Tam wakes — and her magic dies with the stone. Beat: sacrifice and triumph entwined.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash and Lanterns
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Freed souls surface into Ashmoor; Tam, ten years hollow, begins the slow return to himself, guided by the sister he barely remembers. The Guild, leaderless after Corvane's fall, falters. Beat: grief and gratitude.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Charm
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Months later, Mara — magicless — opens a shop with Wendell and Nix, teaching freed souls to live in the light. She has no power and, for the first time, no fear of it. Beat: belonging found, family chosen.
